symptom.description: p95 latency on GET /payments/{id} rose from 140 ms to 610 ms between 09:00 and 09:40 UTC, then recovered without intervention.

users.reason: No user-facing error rate moved; the endpoint stayed within its 2 s timeout throughout, so degradation may not have been perceptible.

impact.slos: Latency SLO (p95 under 400 ms) breached for 40 minutes, consuming 6% of the monthly budget.

probable_cause.reason: Latency rose across every handler at once with no deploy, no traffic change and no database contention; nothing in the collected telemetry distinguishes a cause, and the node-level metrics for the window were not retained.

confidence_rationale: No candidate cause survived the available evidence. Reported as low rather than medium because the leading hypothesis, noisy-neighbour contention, could not be checked at all.

evidence.description: p95 on GET /payments/{id} 140 ms to 610 ms, recovering at 09:40 with no deploy in the window.
pg_stat_statements shows no change in mean execution time for the endpoint's three queries during the window.

commit.reason: No deploy occurred within 36 hours of the window, so no commit is implicated.

expected_change.statement: p95 on GET /payments/{id} stays under 400 ms across a full business day.
expected_change.how_to_verify: The payments-api latency dashboard in Datadog, over one full weekday.

ruled_out.why: Mean and p99 execution times in pg_stat_statements were flat for every query the endpoint issues.
The last deploy to payments-api was 36 hours before the window.

unknowns.question: Whether the node hosting the pods was contended by another workload.
unknowns.why_unresolved: Node-level CPU steal metrics are retained for 6 hours and the window had already aged out when the alert was investigated.

unknowns.question: Whether an upstream dependency slowed down.
unknowns.why_unresolved: The payment processor's status API reports current state only and has no historical endpoint.
